steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease and flour 18 mini muffin cups or line with paper muffin liners.

Stir brown sugar, flour, and pecans together in a medium bowl. Beat butter and eggs together in a separate bowl until smooth; stir into flour mixture until just combined. Spoon batter into the prepared muffin cups about 2/3 full.
Bake muffins in the preheated oven until tops spring back when touched, about 20 to 25 minutes; cool on wire racks.

raw_recipe.headline: Pecan Pie Muffins
raw_recipe.description: These moist pecan pie muffins loaded with chopped pecans and topped with brown sugar have all the flavors of pecan pie for a wonderful holiday treat.
raw_recipe.name: Pecan Pie Muffins

review.reviewBody: I love these muffins! I wound up selling products for a company based out of Texas because I fell in love with the pecan pie muffin mix they had. I was so excited to find a recipe for these wonderful little gems. I only put about 1/2 cup of pecans in mine and I like them pretty gooey so I bake them at 325 degrees for about 12 minutes. They do tend to stick. I use a nonstick mini muffin pan and spray it very well. Baker's joy works better than anything else. I wouldn't recommend using the paper muffin liners. The muffins stick to them like glue.

I have found that the "key" to these muffins is mini muffin tins -- the regular size ones just don't work, and Baker's Joy spray. Also, I fill mine with just 1 tbsp. of filling, and bake only 17 minutes. Mine are always a hit, in fact, I am enjoying some right now. I love the jar gift idea -- I am going to try that one next Christmas.

I’ve made these too many times. Huge hit at potlucks. They mix together quicker than it takes to load the mini muffin tins. I do not grease and flour the tins, I just grease them very well with butter. It makes the outside of them a bit chewy and crispy. I live at a higher altitude now and add an extra tablespoon of flour. Don’t over fill the tins, just 3/4 of the way up. They will overflow the cups. If you’re going to use use a muffin cup I’d use foil not paper, these are a bit sticky.

I toasted the pecans at 325° for 7 minutes before chopping, reduced the brown sugar to 3/4 cup and the butter to just more than 1/2 cup, added 2 tsp each of vanilla and maple syrup and baked for about 22 minutes at 325°. Thanks for a great recipe!

These are delicious! I followed the recipe exactly, except for the addition of 1/2 tsp vanilla, which I will up to 1 tsp next time. I used regular sized muffin tins, as I don't own a mini-muffin tin. My tins are stainless steel, and I sprayed them with bakers joy. Filled each halfway, made 12 muffins, but they are not tall. They don't rise much and end up about the same size as the raw dough you filled them with. They took about 20 minutes to bake, the edges were crispy and I didn't want to over-bake them, so I removed them from the oven and immediately ran a knife around the edges. I used a small silicone spatula to remove them carefully to a wire rack. No sticking whatsoever!
I ate 4 of them within 20 minutes, that says a lot!

These little muffins were delicious after a second attempt with the following changes from original recipe. Use 1/2 cup melted butter instead of 2/3 cup softened butter. Cook for 15 minutes, not 20. Do not use paper liners. Spray mini muffin pan with Bakers Joy non stick baking spray. Recipe makes 24 mini muffins.

Oh my word, how did I miss this recipe? These muffins were fantastic. I followed the recipe exactly except I added 1/4 tsp of vanilla (because vanilla makes everything better). I used paper muffin tins in a silicone mini muffin pan and sprayed them with Pam and everything came out just fine. I also filled the tins 100% full which did not spill over the sides so it left a very pretty, golden brown rounded muffin. I was also able to fill 24 of the mini tins completely full with the batter this recipe produced. So pleased with this recipe. Will be a permanent addition to my bag of tricks.

I previously started my review but accidentally submitted before I completed it. Sorry! I followed the recipe by using softened butter and I slightly beat the eggs. When I tried to mix this it was a total disaster. It was a huge glob. I had to it poured out and start over. I’ll began reading others reviews and made the following alterations. These turned out delicious and addicting! The second time I melted the butter. This is extremely important and added a teaspoon of vanilla to the egg/butter mixture. To the sugar, flour, pecan mixture I added a pinch of salt. I baked them in a dark, nonstick pan that I greased with shortening and dusted with flour. I lowered the temperature to 340 degrees due to a darker pan. I cooked each batch 25 minutes. I waited 2 minutes after I took them out of the oven, then I ran a butter knife around their edges to loosen them. I immediately removed them from the pan and placed them on a cooling rack. Each one lifted out beautifully with no mess! I used a mixture of smaller and larger pieces of pecans in my batter as well. THESE ARE SO DELICIOUS!

Pretty good! Does remind me of Pecan Pie. BF said best muffin he’d ever had. I did replace a bit of brown sugar with white. I used a bit more butter. Added vanilla and salt. Made mini muffins and no liners. Just sprayed with non-stick and sprinkled with a bit of sugar. Minimal sticking. Baked 15m @ 350.

These are tasty, and pretty simple to make. I replaced about a quarter of the flour with oats, which worked well and gave them a nice texture. I greased and floured my muffin pans, and didn't have a problem with them sticking. Next time I'll probably try reducing the butter and sugar a little, since they are VERY rich, and perhaps using half oats instead of a quarter. Be aware that these are desserts in muffin shape!

Wonderful rich crunchy pecan flavor. My hubby who isn't a pecan fan though they were "really good" and "not too sweet". (Next time, I'm trying toasted walnuts instead of pecans just to change it up.). Listening to other reviewers, I buttered and floured my non-stick mini muffin tins and the muffins came right out after sitting in the tin for a couple of minutes after baking. I also added 1/2 tsp salt to enhance the flavors and a 1/2 tsp vanilla. I baked them for 20 minutes and got a nice crunch to the outside yet tender in the middle. Next time I'm going to reduce the baking time to try some that are still gooey in the middle as also suggested by reviewers. That would make them even more pecan pie like! Thanks for a versatile, easy and pantry friendly muffin recipe!
I made It using unsalted butter because It did not state what kind of butter to use. It turned out tasting pretty gross with no salt. Plan to try It again using salt this time we will see.

I’m not a fan of pecan pie really, but I made these for my kids and they are addicting! I ate 3 lol. They’re crunchy AND soft and taste just like pecan pie with only a few ingredients! Will definitely be making these a lot from now on. Thanks for sharing!

I’ve been making these for over a decade as they are a family favorite. I add a teaspoon of vanilla and about a quarter teaspoon salt. The only change I make is if my eggs are actually large, I only use 1 as I find with how little flour there is they can become quite eggy tasting.
Favourite go-to for family and friends! I doubled the quantity of pecans - absolutely decadent! Next, I want to make them gluten and dairy free, which will be a challenge, so any advice is welcome.
Love love love this recipe. So easy also... Mother in law

I used sugar free brown sugar (takes only half the amount). Added a bit of baking powder, cinnamon and vanilla. Before using the pecans I sautéed pecans in a butter and oil infusion. I saved some to garnish the tops. Used the remainder in the recipe. I liked the flavor and muffin consistency. Thank you.
Little too sweet for me. But else excellent! And do spray the paper cups. These are very sticky.
